transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, I guess... what finally scared me enough to come in is that I just keep thinking it would be a relief if I went to sleep and didn't wake up. I haven't actually tried to hurt myself or anything like that, but... those thoughts are just there, and it's frightening me.
How long have you been feeling this way?
It's been going on for about four months now. I guess... yeah, it started right around the time my aunt came to live with us.
Are you experiencing other symptoms, such as a significant change in your appetite, your sleep patterns, or your ability to concentrate?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I'm eating about the same as I always do, and... well, my sleep seems fine. I can still focus on things okay, I suppose. It's really just those thoughts I told you about.
Do you find that you have been feeling particularly anxious, nervous, or worried since your aunt moved in?
No, I wouldn't say that. I mean... I don't really feel nervous or worried or anything like that. It's really just those thoughts about going to sleep that I mentioned.
Aside from those thoughts about not wanting to wake up, have you been feeling a persistent sense of sadness or tearfulness since your aunt moved in?
Yeah, I have. Most mornings... I just wake up with this heavy sadness right in my chest. It feels like, well, like I've already failed the day before it even starts.
Have you noticed any physical sensations like heart racing, trembling, or muscle tension since your aunt moved in?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I don't get the shakes, and my heart isn't racing or... or anything. My body doesn't really feel tense, just... well, just heavy and sad, like I said. But no racing heart or trembling.
Have you noticed any feelings of restlessness or an inability to sit still since your aunt moved in?
No, not really. I don't have any trouble sitting still. I don't feel restless or... fidgety or anything like that. If anything, I mostly just sit in my chair a lot, to be honest.
Have you experienced any persistent feelings of apprehension or dread since your aunt moved in?

No, I haven't really felt anything like that. I don't feel any dread or, you know, apprehension about things. It's just that heavy sadness I mentioned, but not... not a feeling that something bad is about to happen.
Have you noticed any changes in your behavior, such as avoiding certain places or people, or perhaps feeling the need to constantly check on things since your aunt moved in?

No, I haven't started doing anything like that. I don't avoid places or people... well, I mean, I don't go out much anyway, but not because I'm avoiding anything specific. And I don't feel the need to check on things all the time. My behavior hasn't really changed in those ways since she moved in.
Do you ever feel like you are on edge or unable to relax because of your situation?
No, not really. I don't feel on edge or anything. I mean, I'm just mostly tired and sad, like I said. But I don't feel keyed up or like I can't relax. I just kind of sit there, really.
Do you feel like you are struggling to cope with the stress of your aunt's presence in your home?

No, not really. I don't feel stressed out by her being here. I mean, she kind of just does her own thing, and I do mine. It's not like I'm struggling to deal with her... it's just that heavy feeling I have all the time. But no, her being in the house isn't really causing me any extra stress.
How much has this heavy sadness interfered with your ability to carry out your daily tasks or work?

It's gotten in the way quite a bit, honestly. I've actually stopped going to my dance class and my walking group. I haven't been doing my shifts at the food pantry lately, either. I just... I can't seem to get going. And at home, my husband has had to take over a lot more of the errands because I just kind of get stuck. I sit there and just fall behind on everything I'm supposed to be doing.
